label: original-phase input of b/d/h/r/o/i/p/m/f (first occurrence, mid-sequence)
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase: 99.9% of activation mass. It never fires on the delimiter and almost never during the copy phase. Activity peaks at positions t=2-5 (t=3 carries 30% of mass) and is weak at t=0 and t>=7. It responds most to particular input letters: b strongly (rate 35%, 23% of mass, and all the top activations), then d, h, r, o, i, p, m, f. It is mostly a first occurrence of the token (93% of mass has in_first=1). Rate is somewhat higher when earlier inputs include 1/t/w/v/y/c/n, but adding that condition did not improve F1. Even the best case (first b at t=2-6) is active only about 62% of the time, so the hidden-state history modulates it in ways a simple predicate does not capture. The predicate catches about 80% of activation mass on dev but has low precision (about 0.35).
